title: Source tax tariff: denomination, spouse employment and tariff code
purpose: Ask for denomination and whether the spouse or partner works. Combine these with the child digit and the cross-border result into the full Zurich tariff code, which replaces HR's manual calculator step.

stories.title: Ask the religious denomination only where source tax needs it and derive the church-tax suffix
stories.i_want: the employee's religious denomination to be asked only from employees who are subject to source tax and need a tariff code, and turned into the church-tax part of the tariff code
stories.so_that: the tariff code ends in the correct church-tax suffix (Y or N), while employees who are not subject to source tax are not asked about their religion
stories.priority_reason: The denomination is part of every tariff code Lonio computes in place of HR's manual calculator step (D-001); without it no tariff code can be produced. Asking it of everybody would collect sensitive data no party needs (G-01, F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination is asked only when a tariff code is needed
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee filling in the onboarding questionnaire, whose answers on residence, nationality, C permit, civil status and spouse decide whether they are subject to source tax (rule 'Subject to source tax'); for employees living in Liechtenstein, the questions on daily return and on more than 45 non-return days come first
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire reaches the source tax tariff questions
acceptance_criteria.then: the denomination is asked and required only if the employee is subject to source tax and, for an employee living in Liechtenstein, only if they do not return daily and expect more than 45 non-return days. In all other cases it is not asked. The question order and skipping for Liechtenstein residents is an assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-040).

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination answers offered
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee chooses exactly one of 'Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' or 'None or other'; no other denominations are offered, and the answer is recorded for the source tax tariff determination

acceptance_criteria.title: Church-tax suffix follows the denomination
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax who has answered the denomination
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the church-tax suffix of the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: the suffix is Y for 'Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed' and N for 'None or other'

stories.title: Ask married employees and registered partners subject to source tax whether their spouse or partner works
stories.i_want: married employees and employees in a registered partnership who need a tariff code to say whether their spouse or registered partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income
stories.so_that: the tariff letter can be set to C or B, as the calculator does for married persons
stories.priority_reason: HR names the spouse's employment as a question that changes the calculator result (F-hr_transcript-6a0a40); without it no tariff code can be computed for married employees (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse employment is asked only of married employees and registered partners who need a tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who is subject to source tax (rule 'Subject to source tax') and, if living in Liechtenstein, does not return daily and expects more than 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee's civil status is Married or Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.then: the question 'Is your spouse or registered partner gainfully employed or receiving replacement income?' is asked and required, with the answers yes or no. It is not asked of single, divorced, widowed or separated employees, nor of employees who need no tariff code. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: for source tax a registered partnership counts as married and separated counts as single, as in the calculator (D-003). For Liechtenstein residents this question comes after the daily-return and 45-day questions (assumption, D-040).

acceptance_criteria.title: Answer recorded for source tax only
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse employment question is answered
acceptance_criteria.then: the answer is recorded for the source tax tariff determination only; the employee is not asked for the spouse's income type or amount (a new employee's own income is always earned income, D-006)

stories.title: Derive the base source tax tariff letter
stories.i_want: Lonio to derive the base tariff letter (A, B, C or H) from the employee's civil status, the spouse's employment and the children
stories.so_that: I no longer have to click through the Zurich calculator to find the tariff letter
stories.priority_reason: Today HR determines the tariff by hand in the calculator (F-hr_transcript-34494f); the product decision is that Lonio computes it (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Base letter for married employees and registered partners
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax whose civil status is Married or Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is C if the spouse or registered partner is gainfully employed or receives replacement income, and B if not. Children do not change the letter, only the child digit. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: a registered partnership counts as married for source tax (D-003).

examples.name: Married, spouse works, minor child with sole custody

acceptance_criteria.title: Base letter for single, divorced, separated and widowed employees
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax whose civil status is Single, Divorced, Separated or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is H if at least one child counts with H (per-child result, owned by the children section), otherwise A. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: separated counts as single for source tax (D-003).

acceptance_criteria.title: No replacement-income or special tariffs
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the base tariff letter
acceptance_criteria.then: the letter is always one of A, B, C or H; the replacement-income tariffs G and Q and special tariffs such as D (second job) never result, because a new employee always has earned income and special tariffs are out of scope for onboarding

stories.title: Replace the base letter with the cross-border letter where the cross-border tariff applies
stories.i_want: the base tariff letter to be replaced by its cross-border letter when the cross-border tariff applies to an employee living in Germany
stories.so_that: cross-border commuters from Germany get the same tariff letter the calculator would give them
stories.priority_reason: Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax (F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a) and HR finds their calculator path the most complicated (F-hr_transcript-8595fb); Lonio now owns this result (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border letters
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Germany for whom the cross-border tariff applies (rule 'Cross-border tariff applies': daily return with a certificate of residence, or no daily return although daily return is reasonable and no more than 60 non-return days expected)
acceptance_criteria.then: the base letter is replaced: A by L, B by M, C by N, H by P

acceptance_criteria.title: Base letter kept where the normal tariff applies
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee subject to source tax for whom the cross-border tariff does not apply: living in Germany without a certificate of residence ('no' or 'not yet'), or not returning daily where return is not reasonable or more than 60 non-return days are expected, or living in Switzerland, Liechtenstein or any other country
acceptance_criteria.then: the base letter (A, B, C or H) is used unchanged. A certificate answered 'not yet' counts as 'no'; if it is handed in later, HR records it and the letter is derived again (D-035, D-037).

stories.title: Compute and record the full source tax tariff code
stories.i_want: Lonio to compute the full Zurich tariff code (tariff letter, child digit and church-tax suffix, e.g. C1Y or L0Y) for every employee subject to source tax and record it for me
stories.so_that: I no longer click through the Zurich calculator by hand for each new employee
stories.priority_reason: HR currently runs the calculator manually for every source-taxed employee (F-hr_transcript-34494f); replacing this step is an explicit product decision (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Tariff code composed from letter, child digit and suffix
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who is subject to source tax and is not a Liechtenstein resident with daily return or at most 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio records the tariff code written as the tariff letter, followed by the child digit (the number of children who count, 0 without children, no maximum), followed by the church-tax suffix Y or N, for example C1Y or L0Y

acceptance_criteria.title: No tariff code when not subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee who is not subject to source tax (rule 'Subject to source tax')
acceptance_criteria.then: no tariff code is recorded and none of the tariff questions were asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents: no tariff code or tariff code with treaty note
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Liechtenstein, who has answered the daily-return and, where asked, the more-than-45-days question before any denomination, spouse or children question
acceptance_criteria.then: with daily return, or without daily return and at most 45 non-return days, no tariff code is recorded; instead 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' is recorded and flagged for HR. With more than 45 non-return days the normal tariff code is recorded with the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement' and flagged for HR. How HR sees the flag belongs to the later HR-side spec (see OQ-hr-side-follow-ups). Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-040).

acceptance_criteria.title: Tariff code always follows the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: a submitted questionnaire with a recorded tariff code (or no tariff code)
acceptance_criteria.when: HR later changes an answer it depends on, for example a marriage, a new child, a move or a certificate of residence handed in later
acceptance_criteria.then: the tariff code, and whether one is needed at all, is derived again from the latest answers; the employee cannot change answers after submission. How HR makes such changes belongs to the later HR-side spec.

acceptance_criteria.title: Comparison with the calculator before go-live
acceptance_criteria.given: Lonio's tariff code computation is complete
acceptance_criteria.when: the feature is prepared for release
acceptance_criteria.then: a domain expert compares Lonio's computed tariff codes with the Zurich calculator for the paths not explored (residence block for A/B/H, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N examples and per-child results marked inferred) before go-live; where observed calculator results exist, they win over derived ones. This is a non-blocking go-live condition (see OQ-calculator-coverage). Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-046).
